entry.dc:title: EARLY STAGES OF MINE SOIL GENESIS IN A SOUTHWEST VIRGINIA SPOIL LITHOSEQUENCE.
entry.dc:creator: Roberts J.
entry.prism:publicationName: Soil Science Society of America Journal
entry.dc:description: Natural topsoils in the Appalachian surface mining region are often more difficult to use and less desirable than alternative spoil materials. Parent material effects and initial pedogenic changes over 3 yr were observed in 5 mixes of sandstone (SS) and siltstone (SiS) spoils under grass vegetation. Spoil type controlled initial soil texture, but significant decreases in sand contents and increases in silt contents occurred in several spoil mixes within 2 yr. All mine soils studied were high ( plus or minus 65%) in coarse fragments. Mine soils derived from spoils high in siltstone content were higher in coarse fragments, pH, extractable cations and iron, fine earth ( less than 2 mm) water holding capacity, and electrical conductivity than sandstone mine soils. Dissolution and leaching, oxidation, and organic matter incorporation were dominant pedogenic processes influencing mine soil properties over the period of this experiment.

entry.dc:title: Geotechnical engineering beyond soil mechanics - a case study
entry.dc:creator: Morgenstern N.
entry.dc:description: Geotechnical engineering embraces soil mechanics, rock mechanics, and engineering geology. In practice it employs a wide variety of techniques ranging from site mapping and characterization to advanced theoretical analysis and performance monitoring. This paper draws on the development of the Alberta oil sands as a case study to illustrate the breadth of application of geotechnical engineering in large-scale resource developments. A description of the resource base and common extractive procedures used in the Alberta oil sands is given. The geological setting and geotechnical characterization of the Athabasca deposit are summarized. Detailed discussions are presented on geotechnical contributions to surface mining and slope stability, waste handling and tailings dam construction, and in situ recovery processes. The substantial opportunities for geotechnical engineering to contribute to both safe and economical operations in the extractive industries are emphasized. -Authors

entry.dc:title: Mining and landscape modification on the Sydney coalfield
entry.dc:creator: Millward H.
entry.prism:publicationName: Geographical Perspectives on the Maritime Provinces
entry.dc:description: Cape Breton's Sydney coalfield has been worked continuously since 1720. This paper describes the cumulative impact of underground and surface mining as evidenced in today's land use pattern and visual landscape. Particular attention is paid to the effects of recent environmental improvement policies. -Author

entry.dc:title: Continuous haulage and in-pit crushing in surface mining
entry.dc:creator: Terezopoulos N.G.
entry.dc:description: The paper discusses the use of high speed, side-slewable belt conveyors in large-scale surface mining, in conjunction with in-pit crushing. The reasons for the use of such a transport system are discussed and compared to other systems. Bucket Chain Excavators (BCE), or Bucket Wheel Excavators (BWE) used in surface mining can only be fully utilised with a continuous transport system, such as a conveyor belt. Loading of the belts is carried out by the excavators in the pit and the spoil is taken around the pit to the spoil bank. In cases where the overburden is thick and competent, pre-stripping and crushing are required, to enable the use of belt conveyors for transport. The application criteria and the method of use of such systems are described, and economical factors are considered. © 1988 Elsevier Science Publishers B.V.

entry.dc:title: AGGREGATE RESOURCES - CALIFORNIA'S EFFORT UNDER SMARA TO ENSURE THEIR CONTINUED AVAILABILITY.
entry.dc:creator: Beeby D.
entry.dc:description: California's Surface Mining and Reclamation Act (SMARA) was passed in 1975 to identify and protect mineral resources in areas of high land use conflict and ensure reclamation of mined lands. Under SMARA, aggregate resource availability is quantified and compared to forecast demand in specific market regions. Fifteen regions studied thus far cover 51,800 km**2 (20,000 sq miles) and contain 45 Gt (50 billion st) of high-quality aggregate resources that have been legally designated as regionally significant, providing a measure of protection previously unavailable. SMARA reports and state testimony at local hearings have supplied objective information and helped reduce conflict in mine permitting decisions.

entry.dc:title: LAND SHAPING AND SOIL CONSTRUCTION.
entry.dc:creator: Jansen I.
entry.dc:description: Reclamation after surface mining or other drastic land disturbance involves shaping the land surface and constructing a soil. One must begin by selecting a land use objective. Considerations are local needs and potential for constructing the needed supporting land resource. Use objectives determine land resource needs, but available materials and material handling equipment limit the kind of soil resource that can be constructed and hence the land use options that can be considered. A reasonable reclamation objective would be to construct a land resource of maximum feasible utility and versatility for future generations. Utility implies concern that it not only have some productive use, but that it complement other land resource that is capable of multiple uses, to keep options open for future generations. Cost is one consideration under feasibility, at least to the extent that a significant increase in the utility or versatility of the finished product should result from any reclamation practice of significant cost.

entry.dc:title: PYRITIC MATERIALS: ACID DRAINAGE, SOIL ACIDITY, AND LIMING.
entry.dc:creator: Caruccio F.
entry.dc:description: Sulfide minerals, when exposed to the atmosphere, can form acid sulfate soils and acidic-, ferrous-, and sulfate-enriched drainage water. These conditions generally arise from the oxidation of iron disulfides exposed by surface mining. Rock analyses can provide a first approximation of the anticipated acidity characteristics of the overburden and anticipated drainage quality. Pyrite oxidation products are readily soluble in water and hydrolyze to produce acidic waters which severely impact drainage systems. Acid sulfate weathering as a result of pyrite oxidation can produce acid sulfate soils. Recognition of the potential for formation of acid sulfate soils, measurement of the forms of soil acidity, and deep burial or neutralization of that acidity are essential if establishment and sustained growth of plants are to be achieved. The above data illustrate several points regarding the liming of acid sulfate soils. First, using the appropriate analytical methods, total lime requirements can be calculated. Second, application of adequate amounts of lime to neutralize the active acidity as well as the potential acidity is feasible in these systems, particularly if CaCO//3 is the lime source.

entry.dc:title: RELATION OF PUBLIC POLICY TO RECLAMATION GOALS AND RESPONSIBILITIES.
entry.dc:creator: Doll E.
entry.dc:description: The enactment of the Surface Mining Control and Reclamation Act of 1977 or SMCRA (PL 95-87) set federal standards for the reclamation of lands disturbed by surface mining for coal. This act provides guidelines and regulatory procedures under which the industry is responsible for the reclamation of surface-mines lands; costs of reclamation are passed on to the consumer. Compliance with these provisions has required major changes in mining practices and reclamation techniques. The coal industry has accepted this responsibility, and surface-mined lands have generally been successfully reclaimed. Reclamation planning cannot become static; it must be flexible and responsive to changes in public needs and policy and to the development of more efficient and cost-effective reclamation techniques. In the discussion, the author attempts to evaluate the reclamation goals and practices in this context. A brief review of the changing attitude toward public responsibilities for reclamtion of surface-mined land, which led to the enactment of federal legislation, is given to place the discussion in proper context.

entry.dc:title: CORRECTION OF PHYSICAL LIMITATIONS TO RECLAMATION.
entry.dc:creator: Barnhisel R.
entry.dc:description: The physical properties of disturbed soils are changed as the result of surface mining. These changes may be beneficial to future land use when the surface-mine operator uses proper techniques and takes advantage of selecting more desirable materials for the restored soil than existed in the natural soil. Perhaps more frequently, the physical properties of the restored soils are degraded during mining. The degradation may result from mixing undesirable soil horizons together, as well as excessive soil compaction which often occurs in the removal and reconstruction process. These physical limitations often result in poorer root penetration into the replace soil, thereby reducing plant growth. The possible effects on plant growth of such changes in the physical properties during surface mining are presented. Methods of reducing such occurrences, ways of recognizing them, and possible methods for correcting them are discussed.

entry.dc:title: LESS CONVENTIONAL METHODS FOR MINING UNDERGROUND COAL.
entry.dc:creator: Muirhead I.
entry.dc:description: In recent years, mining considerations and economics have encouraged a transition from underground mining to surface mining. However, a change in market conditions or the development of superior underground mining methods may reverse this trend. This paper reports on a CANMET-funded examination of less conventional underground coal mining methods. These methods are documented and those that show the most promise for application to western Canadian conditions are discussed in detail.

entry.dc:title: RESOURCES RECOVERABLE BY SURFACE MINING.
entry.dc:creator: Doolittle J.J.
entry.dc:description: The methods used to mine mineral resources can be separated into two broad categories: surface and underground. Both of these mining methods cause a 'disturbance' at the earth's surface; however, in surface mining all of the soil and strata overlying a mineral deposit are removed to expose the deposit. This procedure disturbs more surface acreage than in underground mining where the mineral deposit is removed from beneath intact surface layers. Of the major mineral resources in the U. S. , 11 are totally or partially removed by surface mining: bauxite, coal, clay, copper, gypsum, iron, limestone/dolomite, molybdenum, phosphate rock, sand/gravel, and uranium. Oil shale will also be recovered by surface mining when it becomes economically feasible to extract oil products from it. These minerals are discussed in more detail in this paper. Most of the information within this paper adheres to the system of classification of mineral deposits jointly developed by the U. S. Bureau of Mines and U. S. Geological Survey.

entry.dc:title: Discrimination of factors influencing biota of a stream receiving multiple-source perturbations
entry.dc:creator: Van Hassel J.H.
entry.dc:description: Blaine Creek is a fifth-order stream located in eastern Kentucky that has been subject to contamination by oil brines, surface mining, and a coal fly ash settling pond discharge. Toxicity tests, effluent and receiving water chemical monitoring, and Blaine Creek benthic sampling were used to evaluate the effect of the ash pond effluent on the creek. Reproductive impairment of Ceriodaphnia was demonstrated at effluent concentrations ranging from 30 to 100%, but no instream impact on benthic invertebrates could be found at effluent flows that provided up to 65% of the creek's discharge. Correlation and regression analysis of physicochemical versus benthic monitoring data indicated that upstream oil brine contamination and scouring of the creek's predominately shifting sand substrate during rainfall events were the primary factors affecting the benthic fauna, and appeared to override potential effects from other sources. These results demonstrated the value of integrated field/laboratory investigations for effluent impact assessments. © 1988.

entry.dc:title: DEM-determination in lignite surface mining - test for digital image correlation
entry.dc:creator: Boochs F.
entry.dc:description: The automatic DEM-determination by digital image correlation is tested in the case of a stereo-model of lignite surface mining. The special reason for this test is given by the characteristic vertical structure of the object connected with small contrast. As expected the success rate for the point determination has been first under the average. By means of a better approximation of the object geometry and a repetition of the correlation the success rate could have been substantially improved. The accuracy of the determination which has been achieved is near to the level of manual measurements. -English summary

entry.dc:title: Case examples and developments in open pit mine stability
entry.dc:creator: Brawner C.
entry.dc:description: The reduced demand for coals and many minerals has led to substantial advances in geomechanics which are aimed at ensuring efficiency and reduce mining costs. These advances can provide major economic and safety benefits in various areas of surface mining in the near future. Stability on surface mining projects is primarily dependent on five factors. These include structural geology, groundwater, blasting and the existence of weak layers, particularly clayey gouge or clay infill. Case examples of stability on many surface mines including coal mines are presented in this paper.

entry.dc:title: CURRENT SURFACE MINING TECHNIQUES.
entry.dc:creator: Bullivant D.
entry.dc:description: The paper looks at the present position regarding the status of surface mining operations throughout the world compared with underground mining and examines the various continuous conveying techniques available to overcome the problems encountered in developing various types of geological deposits. A case is put for the employment of a skilled engineering supplier/contractor to effectively integrate the various elements into an efficient system of material transportation.

entry.dc:title: Intersection graphic method - a method for calculating quantity of coal and rock by using a computer for selection of surface mining schemes
entry.dc:creator: Tian H.
entry.prism:publicationName: Meitan Xuebao Journal of the China Coal Society
entry.dc:description: This paper proposes a method based on the exhaustion method for calculating the quantity of coal and rock by using a computer for selecting an optimal surface mining scheme provides a mathematical model for the calculations. The system adopts the template technique for producing frustum files. This system has improved the accuracy of calculation by separating different zone so that a variable slope can be varied at different azimuths and depths within the boundary of a surface mine.

entry.dc:title: NEW TECHNOLOGY FOR LARGE SURFACE MINES.
entry.dc:creator: Singhal R.
entry.dc:description: High-volume surface mining operations such as the Canadian oil sands mines depend on high-capacity equipment for excavation and transportation of overburden and ore. Dragline and bucket wheel excavator/conveyor systems have been developed to high levels of productivity, and numerous improvements have been made in all phases of mining practice. However, mines throughout the world continue to devote considerable effort to developing innovative new technologies, operating techniques, and procedures for improving productivity. Operators of such mines should periodically prepare an awareness report, evaluating outside technology for in-house use. This type of intelligence and technology transfer is vital to maintenance of competitive and cost effective operations. This article briefly reviews some technology and operating practices that have recently become available to large-scale surface mines.

entry.dc:title: AMAX TAKES ITS DELTA SURFACE MINE UNDERGROUND.
entry.dc:creator: Trewhitt J.
entry.dc:description: Amax Coal Co. has brought longer life to a former section of its Delta surface mine near Harrisburg, Ill. , by punching entries into the highwall to form a 500,000-tpy underground mine. Delta's mined-out Harco section has been transformed into the company's first highwall mine. If the mine succeeds, the company might create other underground mines when surface operations reach their economic limits. At Harco, surface mining stopped when the overburden to coal ratio reached 24. 27:1.

entry.dc:title: COMPUTER-AIDED BLAST DESIGNS SUCCEED IN SURFACE MINING.
entry.dc:creator: Chironis N.
entry.dc:description: Blasting simulation programs have been developed that can permit almost any blasting procedure in the field to be tried first as a simulated event in the computer. One of the programs is Du Pont's Computer Simulated Blasting (CSB) program. Based on the Blaspa method, the program has been used in more than 50 mines and quarries to simulate blasting conditions. The CSB program is based on a mathematical model that takes into account site-specific conditions such as type of explosive, rock type, blast geometry and drilling patterns. The program predicts the results of the blast and lets the blaster alter the input variables one at a time.

entry.dc:title: A case study in surface mining simulation with special reference to the problem of model evaluation
entry.dc:creator: Ogbonlowo D.B.
entry.prism:publicationName: International Journal of Mining and Geological Engineering
entry.dc:description: This paper discusses the framework for modelling and analysing the materials handling aspects of a conventional contour mine as related to the smaller to medium-size coal mining companies. Special emphasis is placed on model evaluation. The methodology employed consists of: (a) using the surface geometry of the area to be stripped for developing the equations that are used for analysing the critical factors affecting pit layout, (b) effecting engineering and graphical layout of the mine, (c) collecting - through time studies - and analysing equipment characteristic data, (d) constructing the model, and (e) evaluating the model. The results show that the graphical approach for model construction and evaluation is fast, accurate, and reliable. © 1987 Chapman and Hall Ltd.

entry.dc:title: MOWING OF ANNUAL COLONIZERS TO ENHANCE REVEGETATION AFTER SURFACE MINING.
entry.dc:creator: Iverson L.
entry.dc:description: Mowing of first-year erect, annual, colonizing vegetation (especially Kochia scoparia and Salsola collina) was beneficial in the growth and establishment of wheatgrasses (Agropyron caninum, A. smithii and A. elongatum) on restored mined land in western North Dakota. Sample plots containing primarily Kochia, Salsola and Agropyron spp. It was found that Kochia, densities were reduced to about 2% and biomass to one-third that of the control when the area was mowed in mid-August. Agropyron spp. , however, showed an increase of 860% in biomass production over the control due to mowing in mid-August.

entry.dc:title: MICROPROCESSOR-AIDED EQUIPMENT PROVES PRODUCTIVE AND RELIABLE.
entry.dc:creator: Chironis N.
entry.dc:description: Teamed with miniature sensors and advanced electronic gadgetry, microprocessors are improving the performance of earthmoving equipment and haulers for surface mining operations. The microprocessor may be only about 1 one-half in. wide by 2 in. long, a flat component with a series of I-O's (input-output) prongs on both sides to read sensors feeding into it information on speeds, pressures, temperatures and other machine functions while it sends signals to control a range of components from LED lights to engines. Such microprocessors are being designed into excavators, shovels, scrapers and trucks. The article gives examples.

entry.dc:title: Environmental impact assessment procedure for surface mining projects in India - a status review
entry.dc:creator: Banerjee S.
entry.prism:publicationName: Journal of Mines Metals and Fuels
entry.dc:description: In India, the present system of granting environmental clearance to mining projects has been introduced from early 1982. The Ministry of Environment and Forests has constituted four Environmental Appraisal Committees (EACs) to comment on the environmental impact of large development projects. The mining EAC has representatives from various Government Departments. The Committee has an advisory status only, and makes its recommendations to the Department of Environment, Forests and Wildlife. In fact the requirement of getting an environmental clearance is based on administrative instructions of the Public Investment Board to which the public sector organizations have to apply for getting sanction of fund for new large projects or extension of projects. Another route through which projects get referred to the mining EAC is from the Forestry Wing of the Department of Environment, Forests and Wildlife when request for release of forest land for mining purposes is received by that wing.

entry.dc:title: Blasting in overburden with site mixed slurry - a techno-economic assessment
entry.dc:creator: Sinha A.K.
entry.prism:publicationName: Journal of Mines Metals and Fuels
entry.dc:description: The future years of Indian coal mining will see a significant increase in the production of coal from large mechanized opencast mines and huge quantities of overburden removal by deploying large capacity dragline and other heavy earth moving machinery. To attain overall economics, the very initial operating such as blasting, has to be very much cost efective as well as low manpower intensive. This can be achieved only by bulk handling of explosives and more R&D efforts to generate direct cost reduction in addition to the highest degree of safety. This article highlights investment, annual production capacity, average stripping ratio and the total excavation of overburden of some of the major ongoing surface mining projects in the coal sector of India. Various technical and economical benefits associated with mechanized bulk handling of site-mixed explosive slurries are reviewed.

entry.dc:title: Failure study of dumper tyres in surface mining project
entry.dc:creator: De A.
entry.prism:publicationName: Journal of Mines Metals and Fuels
entry.dc:description: In the present work, an investigation has been undertaken to study the failure of tires. Two opencast projects were considered for the study. Tires were inspected five times and samples were taken on a random basis. Defective tires were inspected visually. The article presents the results of this study. Analysis has been based on statistical methods and failure mode.
